notes: This page only shows assembling a minifigure (red cap, head, red torso with arms and hands, black legs). None of these minifigure parts appear in the supplied parts list or catalogue, so no pieces are recorded.
The Mail Van build itself has not started on this page. Piece ids continue from b1 on the next page that has building steps.

Step 1: the door (b2) hinges onto the red 2x2x2 box (b1). Step 2: the curved 2x2 brick (b3) is on top of the box (shown already fitted), and the two envelope tiles are slid in through the door slot. Step 3: the mailbox is placed on the grey round support (b6). Step 4 shows the finished mailbox with the minifigure.
The box (b1) was placed before the support (b6), so its seat on the support is recorded in other_joins rather than rests_on.
The envelope tiles (b4, b5) are inserted into the box, not clutched onto studs, so rests_on is empty.
Step 1: the red vehicle base (b7) is the first piece. A red 1x4 plate (b8) goes onto the raised side of the base.

Step 2: a yellow 2x2 plate goes on each end recess of the base (b9, b10). Two yellow door-rail plates (b11, b12) go on the base at the left end. The picture shows one already fitted and one being added.

The exact stud cells are not clear from the drawing, so every piece is recorded as resting on the base (b7) only. The yellow plates sit in the base's recessed ends, so they may also touch the 1x4 plate (b8).

Step 3 is seen from underneath. One black wheel-holder plate (b13, b14) is attached under each yellow 2x2 plate (b9, b10) at the ends of the chassis. Their pins stick out sideways for the wheels, which are added later.
Step 4 turns the chassis over (top view, red studs) and puts a yellow 2x2 plate (b15) in the centre recess of the base (b7).
Which black plate goes under which yellow plate is inferred from the drawing.
Step 5 (2x): a trans-yellow round plate goes on the side stud of a yellow headlight brick. Both headlight bricks then go on the door-rail plates at the front end, with the grille brick between them.
Step 6: the first yellow wheel arch (b21) goes on the base next to the headlights.
The grille brick (b20) is assumed to span both door-rail plates (b11, b12), with one headlight on each plate. This is inferred from the drawing.
Step 7: the blue steering stand (b23) and blue seat (b24) go on the centre of the chassis, over the yellow 2x2 plate (b15) and the base (b7).
Step 8: a yellow door-rail plate (b25) goes at the rear, and two trans-red 1x1 plates (b26, b27) are added as tail lights. One is shown being placed and one is already fitted.

Correction: page 6 step 6 shows two yellow wheel arches, but only b21 was recorded there. The second arch (b22, the one at the far side in step 7) is added here so the model has both arches that step 7 shows.
Exact stud cells are not clear from the drawing, so supports are inferred.
Step 9: a yellow 1x4 brick goes along each side of the cab (b28 on the near side, b29 on the far side).

Step 10: a taller yellow 1x4 piece goes on the far side near the front. I recorded it as a 1x4 panel with rounded corners (b30) resting on the far wheel arch (b22). The drawing does not make this identification certain, and the other candidate is a plain 1x4 brick.
Which pieces lie directly underneath each one is inferred from the isometric view.
Step 11 (2x): a 7731 mail sticker goes on a yellow 1x4 panel. There are two copies, one for each side of the cab.

Only one 1x4 panel was left in the parts list, so the second copy is the far-side panel b30 from page 8, which therefore gets its sticker here. The sticker sheet is one part (b32) that provides both stickers.
The near-side copy (b31) is placed on the near-side brick (b28). The yellow 1x1 corner panel (b33) goes on the rear stud of that brick. The second corner panel is expected on a later page.
Which pieces lie directly underneath each one is inferred from the isometric view.
Step 12: the last two yellow wheel arches (b34 on the near side, b35 on the far side) go on the rear of the base.
Step 13: a light grey 1x2x2 panel with studs (b36) goes on the rear deck, with a red 1x2 tile (b37) laid flat next to it. The exact placement of both is inferred from the drawing.
The second yellow corner panel (6231) is not clearly placed on this page, so it is left for a later page.
Step 14: a yellow 2x4 plate (b40) is added on top of the two tall yellow rear blocks.

The two tall yellow 1x2x2 bricks with axle holder (b38 on the near side, b39 on the far side) are already fitted in the step 14 drawing, on either side of the grey panel (b36). They were not shown being added on page 10, so they are recorded here.
The 2x4 plate sits across the studs of both blocks, which is inferred from the arrows. The two blocks sit on the rear wheel arches (b34, b35), which is inferred.
Step 15: two grey doors are fitted into the yellow 1x4x3 window frame to make the rear doors. The frame is then put on the rear edge of the van, below the 2x4 roof plate.
The window frame is recorded as resting on the two rear wheel arches (b34, b35), which is inferred. The doors clutch nothing below them, so rests_on is empty.
Step 16: a yellow 1x3 plate (b45) is put on the rear roof. The windscreen (b44) is already fitted at the front in the drawing, but no step shows it being added, so it is recorded here.
The windscreen is recorded as resting on the two front wheel arch plates (b21, b22). It may also clutch the headlight and grille row or the side panels, which is not certain from the drawing.
The red area on the roof in the drawing looks like the red tile (b37) with a second red piece. I could not identify a second red piece for sure, so none is added.
The 1x3 plate is recorded as resting on the 2x4 roof plate (b40), which is inferred.
Step 17 (4x): a tyre is stretched around each grey wheel, and each wheel goes on a pin of a black wheel-holder plate (b13 at one end, b14 at the other).
Which holder end is the front and which pin each wheel takes is chosen by me, and each wheel is on a different pin.

The finished van in this drawing already shows the sloped cab roof, the antenna, and red roof pieces. No earlier step added these, so the remaining parts (sloped brick, curved wedge brick, lever, 1x3 and 1x4 plates, red tile, jumper plate, corner panel, door-rail plate) are left for later pages.
Step 18: the yellow curved wedge brick (b54) goes on the cab as the roof, over the windscreen and the two side panels. The roof carries an envelope sticker.
The minifigure placed in the driver's seat is not in the parts list or catalogue, so it is not recorded.

The finished-van drawing already shows the rear antenna lever and red roof pieces. Those parts (lever, sloped brick, red tile, red 1x4 plate, 1x3 plate, door-rail plate, jumper plate, corner panel) are still not placed.
The roof support is inferred from the drawing.
Parts inventory page with no building step, so nothing is added.
The element IDs shown here agree with the supplied parts list. The 4x tyre line (4515290) corresponds to the 51011 tyre.
Advertising page showing the City airport sets 7731 to 7734. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
LEGO Club and LEGO shop advertisement. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
LEGO City website advertisement. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
Back cover with a competition and customer-service advertisement. It has no building step, so nothing is added.

These parts from the parts list were never shown being placed: lever 298c02, sloped brick 3037, red tile 3069b, door-rail plate 32028, 1x3 plate 3623, red 1x4 plate 3710, jumper plate 3794a, and corner panel 6231. Some of them appear in the finished-van drawings (antenna lever, red roof pieces, rear corner), so the model is likely missing them. No earlier page explicitly added them.
Several placements were inferred from isometric drawings, and the notes on pages 4 to 15 say which.

The mailbox (b1 to b6) and the van are not connected, and I am keeping them as two separate groups. Page 3 builds the mailbox on its own stand, and the other pages build the van. The booklet's drawings show them standing next to each other, never attached.

The page-by-page record never showed eight parts being placed: red 1x4 plate, red tile, red jumper plate, antenna lever, 1x3 plate, door-rail plate, 2x4 sloped brick and corner panel. They appear in the finished-van drawings (pages 14 and 15), so I add them here to match the parts list.

These placements are guesses from the finished-van drawing: the sloped brick (b61) is the front hood over the headlights and grille. The red 1x4 plate (b55), red jumper plate (b57) and 1x3 plate (b59) are on the rear roof plate (b40), with the antenna lever (b58) on the red plate. The red tile (b56) is on the grey panel (b36), and the second corner panel (b62) is on the far-side brick (b29). The extra door-rail plate (b60) is at the rear of the base (b7).
Each is recorded as resting on the pieces I judged to be under it, which could be wrong in detail. The rear roof is crowded, so one or two of these may belong a layer higher or lower than recorded.
The windscreen (b44) was recorded earlier as resting on the front arch plates. It probably also touches the hood (b61). That was not changed.
The two groups are not a real problem for this set. Set 7731-1 builds two separate models: the mailbox on its round stand (b1 to b6, page 3) and the mail van (b7 onward, pages 4 to 15).
The booklet never joins the mailbox to the van. Page 3 shows the mailbox on its own stand, and page 15 draws it beside the van. Adding any join would invent a connection that does not exist.
So I keep the mailbox and the van as two groups and add no pieces or edges.
